# urlet JSON API reference (/en/docs/api)

- Base path: `/api/v1`
- Authentication (choose one)
  - **Session cookie**: `urlet_session`, issued by `POST /api/v1/auth/login` (the browser form flow uses the same cookie)
  - **API token**: `Authorization: Bearer ur_...` (create one under `/app/account`)
- Requests and responses are `application/json; charset=utf-8`
- Timestamps are always ISO-8601 UTC (`2030-01-31T12:00:00.000Z`); input also accepts
  `2030-01-31T12:00:00Z`, `2030-01-31 12:00`, `2030-01-31`, and similar forms
- JSON responses are always English, whatever UI language the visitor selected
  (see [UI language](#ui-language))

This file is the narrative reference. Every instance also serves a browsable version of the same
API, built from the OpenAPI contract in `openapi/`:

- `GET /docs` — the interactive reference (Scalar), following the visitor's interface language
- `GET /docs/openapi.json` — the English OpenAPI 3.1 contract
- `GET /docs/openapi.zh-TW.json` — the Traditional Chinese contract

The reference is embedded in the binary, so it works on an instance with no outbound network.
`/docs` is a reserved path: no short link may use the slug `docs`.

## Error format [#error-format]

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "validation_error",
    "message": "slug may only contain letters, digits, '-' and '_'",
    "details": { "field": "slug" }
  }
}
```

| HTTP | `code` | Meaning |
|------|--------|---------|
| 400 | `bad_request` | Malformed request, or nothing to change |
| 400 | `captcha_failed` | Bot verification failed, expired, or was rejected by the provider (registration and sign-in) |
| 401 | `unauthorized` | Not authenticated, token revoked, wrong password |
| 403 | `forbidden` | Insufficient permission, CSRF rejection, registration closed, quota exhausted |
| 404 | `not_found` | Resource does not exist (including resources that belong to someone else) |
| 409 | `conflict` | Uniqueness conflict (email, slug on a domain, domain hostname) |
| 410 | `gone` | Short link expired or reached its click limit |
| 422 | `validation_error` | Field validation failed; `details.field` names the offending field |
| 429 | `rate_limited` | Rate limited; the response carries a `Retry-After` header |
| 500 | `internal_error` | Server error (details go to the log only) |

Pagination envelope:

```json
{ "items": [], "page": 1, "per_page": 20, "total": 0, "total_pages": 1 }
```

`per_page` defaults to 20 and is capped at 100.

---

## Authentication [#authentication]

### `POST /api/v1/auth/register` [#post-apiv1authregister]

```json
{ "email": "user@example.com", "password": "at-least-8-chars", "invite_code": "optional", "display_name": "optional", "captcha_token": "optional" }
```

`201` → `{ "user": { ... } }`, and the response sets a session cookie (registering signs you in).

Errors: `409` duplicate email, `422` validation failure, `403` registration closed or invalid
invite code, `400` `captcha_failed` when bot verification is enabled and rejects the request.

An invite code may carry a user group. In `invite` mode a code is mandatory; in `open` mode it is
optional, but when one is supplied it is validated and its group wins over the default group. The
returned `user` object includes `group_id`.

The web form accepts the same code as `/app/register?invite=CODE`; the link produced for an invite
prefills the field. The JSON body is unchanged.

`captcha_token` carries the token produced by the CAPTCHA widget on the web registration form.
It is only checked when bot verification is enabled for registration; otherwise the field is
ignored. See [Bot verification](#bot-verification).

> `POST /api/v1/urls` is exempt from bot verification **only when it authenticates with an API
> token** (`Authorization: Bearer ur_...`), so automation and CI pipelines are unaffected. A
> request authenticated with a **session cookie** is a browser session and is subject to the
> link-creation switch; send the widget token in `captcha_token`.

### `POST /api/v1/auth/login` [#post-apiv1authlogin]

```json
{ "email": "user@example.com", "password": "...", "captcha_token": "optional" }
```

`200` → `{ "user": { ... } }` + `Set-Cookie`.
Errors: `401` wrong credentials (the message is fixed and does not reveal whether the account
exists), `403` account suspended, `400` `captcha_failed` when bot verification is enabled for
sign-in and rejects the request, `429` rate limited.

`captcha_token` carries the token produced by the CAPTCHA widget on the web sign-in form. It is
only checked when bot verification is enabled for sign-in (`captcha_on_login` /
`URLET_CAPTCHA_ON_LOGIN`); otherwise the field is ignored. See
[Bot verification](#bot-verification).

### `POST /api/v1/auth/logout` [#post-apiv1authlogout]

`204`, revokes the current session and clears the cookie (may be called anonymously).

### `GET /api/v1/auth/me` [#get-apiv1authme]

`200` → the user, the group they belong to (or `null`) and the effective limits:

```json
{
  "user": { "id": 7, "email": "ada@example.com", "role": "user", "group_id": 2, "...": "..." },
  "group": { "id": 2, "name": "Pro" },
  "limits": {
    "max_urls": 500,
    "max_api_tokens": 5,
    "allow_custom_slug": true,
    "allow_password": true,
    "allow_expiry": true,
    "allow_max_clicks": true,
    "allow_tags": true,
    "allow_api_tokens": true,
    "allow_domain_selection": true,
    "redirect_mode_policy": "choice",
    "default_domain": "links.example.com",
    "allowed_domains": ["links.example.com", "go.example.com"]
  }
}
```

`group` is `null` for an ungrouped account, which falls back to the site-wide settings. The
`limits` object is the resolved value: a group overrides a quota only when it is not `NULL`, and
`0` means unlimited. `default_domain` is the effective group default (falling back to the site
default when it is missing or disabled); `allowed_domains` is the effective selection list. When
`allow_domain_selection` is `false`, only that default is accepted for new links or moves.
`redirect_mode_policy` is `direct`, `splash` or `choice`; it limits the redirect mode of **new**
links and never rewrites existing ones. An ungrouped account gets `choice`.

### `PATCH /api/v1/auth/me` [#patch-apiv1authme]

```json
{ "display_name": "Ada" }
```

An empty string or `null` clears the display name. `200` → `{ "user": { ... } }`

### `POST /api/v1/auth/password` [#post-apiv1authpassword]

```json
{ "current_password": "...", "new_password": "..." }
```

`204`. On success every **other** session is revoked (the current one survives) **and all API
tokens for the account are revoked**.
Errors: `401` wrong current password, `422` new password does not meet the policy.

### `GET /api/v1/auth/sessions` [#get-apiv1authsessions]

`200` → `{ "items": [ { "id", "user_agent", "created_at", "last_seen_at", "expires_at", "current", "revoked" } ] }`

Sessions slide: any activity (written at most once per minute) pushes `expires_at` forward and
re-issues the cookie, so continuous use never expires.

### `DELETE /api/v1/auth/sessions/{id}` [#delete-apiv1authsessionsid]

`204`. You can only revoke your own sessions; anything else is `404`.

### `GET /api/v1/tokens` · `POST /api/v1/tokens` · `DELETE /api/v1/tokens/{id}` [#get-apiv1tokens--post-apiv1tokens--delete-apiv1tokensid]

`POST` body: `{ "name": "ci pipeline", "expires_at": "2030-01-01" }`

`201` → the plaintext token is shown **this one time only**:

```json
{
  "token": "ur_XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX",
  "api_token": { "id": 1, "name": "ci pipeline", "prefix": "ur_abc12345", "scopes": "...", "created_at": "...", "last_used_at": null, "expires_at": "2030-01-01T00:00:00.000Z", "revoked": false, "active": true }
}
```

`DELETE` → `204`.

Token creation is refused with `403` when the group disables API tokens (`allow_api_tokens`) or
the effective `max_api_tokens` is exhausted. Only usable tokens count (not revoked, not expired),
so revoking one frees a slot immediately.

---

## Short links [#short-links]

### `GET /api/v1/urls` [#get-apiv1urls]

Query parameters:

| Parameter | Meaning |
|-----------|---------|
| `q` | Search slug, title and target URL (`%` and `_` are treated literally) |
| `tag` | Filter by tag name |
| `status` | `active` or `disabled` |
| `sort` | `created_at` (default, newest first), `clicks` / `clicks_desc`, `slug` / `slug_asc`, `updated` / `updated_desc`, `expires` / `expires_asc`; each key has one fixed direction and an unknown value falls back to newest first |
| `page` / `per_page` | Pagination |

`200` → a paginated array of `UrlDto`.

### `POST /api/v1/urls` [#post-apiv1urls]

```json
{
  "target_url": "example.com/path",
  "domain": "go.example.com",
  "slug": "promo",
  "title": "Launch",
  "notes": "internal note",
  "tags": ["campaign", "docs"],
  "password": "linkpass",
  "expires_at": "2030-06-30 12:00",
  "max_clicks": 500,
  "redirect_type": 302,
  "redirect_mode": "splash",
  "splash_delay_seconds": 7,
  "splash_title": "Launch day",
  "splash_message": "Welcome aboard",
  "captcha_token": "0.abc..."
}
```

`201` → `UrlDto`. Rules:

- `captcha_token` is only read when the request is authenticated with a **session cookie** and
  bot verification is enabled for link creation; a `Bearer` token call ignores it. A failed
  check returns `400` with `error.code = "captcha_failed"`
- `target_url` is required; only `http`/`https` are accepted, and a bare domain without a scheme
  is given a `https://` prefix
- `domain` may be omitted (the effective group default is used). A supplied hostname must be an
  active domain, otherwise the request fails with `422`; it must also satisfy the group policy
  (`allow_domain_selection`, `restrict_domains` / `domain_ids`) or the request fails with `403`.
  The slug namespace is per domain, so the same slug can exist on two domains
- `slug` may be omitted (a base62 slug of the configured `default_slug_length` is generated,
  4–16 characters, default 7); only `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` is
  allowed, length 1–64, and reserved words are rejected. A slug already used **on the selected
  domain** returns `409`
- `expires_at` must be in the future; `max_clicks` ≥ 1
- `redirect_type` ∈ {301, 302, 307, 308}
- `redirect_mode` is `direct` (default) or `splash`. Omitted, it takes the group policy's default
  (splash under a splash-only policy, otherwise direct). A mode the group blocks returns `403`
- `splash_delay_seconds` is 1–60 (default 5). `splash_title` (at most 120 characters) and
  `splash_message` (at most 500 characters, newlines allowed) are optional; empty/omitted uses the
  localised built-in copy. They are stored even while the link is direct, so switching modes keeps
  the copy
- Exceeding the `max_urls_per_user` quota → `403`

### `GET /api/v1/urls/{id}` [#get-apiv1urlsid]

`200` → `UrlDto` (`state` is `active` / `expired` / `limit_reached` / `disabled`).

### `PATCH /api/v1/urls/{id}` [#patch-apiv1urlsid]

Partial update. A field that is **absent** stays unchanged. An explicit `null` clears only the
nullable fields that opt into it — `title`, `notes`, `password`, `expires_at`, `max_clicks`,
`splash_title` and `splash_message`. For `slug`, `domain`, `status`, `redirect_type`,
`redirect_mode`, `splash_delay_seconds` and `tags`, `null` is treated like an absent field and
keeps the current value.

```json
{ "title": "New title", "domain": "links.example.com", "password": null, "max_clicks": null, "tags": ["new"], "status": "disabled" }
```

`200` → the updated `UrlDto`. An empty object → `400`. Moving a link to another active domain
must satisfy the group policy and re-checks the slug there (`409` on a collision). Keeping a link
on its current domain — even a disabled one — is always allowed, so existing links remain
editable.

### `DELETE /api/v1/urls/{id}` [#delete-apiv1urlsid]

`204`, soft delete. The slug is retained and never released (so old links cannot be hijacked),
and analytics data is kept.

### `GET /api/v1/urls/{id}/stats?days=30` [#get-apiv1urlsidstatsdays30]

```json
{
  "url": { ... },
  "summary": { "total_clicks": 42, "human_clicks": 41, "unique_clicks": 3, "bot_clicks": 1, "first_click_at": "...", "last_click_at": "..." },
  "daily": [ { "day": "2026-02-01", "clicks": 5, "unique_clicks": 2, "bot_clicks": 0 } ],
  "referrers": [ { "label": "news.example.com", "count": 34 } ],
  "devices": [], "browsers": [], "operating_systems": []
}
```

`days` ranges from 1 to 365 (default 30), and `daily` is padded with the days that had no clicks.

### `GET /api/v1/urls/{id}/clicks?page=1` [#get-apiv1urlsidclickspage1]

`200` → a paginated click log (**no** IP addresses or visitor hashes). `page` and `per_page` are
accepted; `per_page` defaults to 20 and is capped at 100:

```json
{ "items": [ { "clicked_at": "...", "referrer_host": "news.example.com", "country_code": null, "device_type": "Desktop", "browser": "Chrome", "os": "Windows", "is_bot": false, "is_unique": true, "password_protected": false } ], "page": 1, "per_page": 20, "total": 42, "total_pages": 3 }
```

### `UrlDto` [#urldto]

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "domain": "s.example.com",
  "slug": "promo",
  "short_url": "https://s.example.com/promo",
  "target_url": "https://example.com/landing",
  "title": "Launch",
  "notes": null,
  "tags": ["campaign"],
  "has_password": true,
  "expires_at": "2030-06-30T12:00:00.000Z",
  "expires_in": "in 52 months",
  "max_clicks": 500,
  "click_count": 42,
  "unique_click_count": 3,
  "redirect_type": 302,
  "redirect_mode": "splash",
  "splash_delay_seconds": 7,
  "splash_title": "Launch day",
  "splash_message": "Welcome aboard",
  "status": "active",
  "is_expired": false,
  "state": "active",
  "is_custom_slug": true,
  "last_clicked_at": "2026-02-11T09:00:00.000Z",
  "created_at": "...",
  "updated_at": "..."
}
```

**Group limits.** Link creation is refused with `403` when the effective `max_urls` is exhausted.
A group feature toggle blocks submitting the matching field on create (`slug`, `password`,
`expires_at`, `max_clicks`, `tags`) and refuses to newly enable it on `PATCH`. Omitting a field
keeps its current value, and clearing a blocked field is accepted; a non-empty link password is
always a new value and is refused while passwords are blocked. The redirect-mode policy blocks a
new `redirect_mode` (or switching to it on `PATCH`) but accepts keeping the current mode and
clearing splash copy.

---

## SNS preview cards [#sns-preview-cards]

Administrators control `preview_image_policy` at `/app/admin/settings` or with `PUT /api/v1/admin/settings`: `{"preview_image_policy":"none"}`. Values: `none` (no images), `url` (HTTPS URLs only), `upload` (uploads only), `both` (default). Invalid values return 422 without partial updates. The policy applies to administrators and members alike; API attempts to set a prohibited source return 403, and browser forms return a 422 retry page retaining text. Keeping/removing an image and editing text remain allowed. Existing disallowed images stay stored but are omitted from metadata and the response `image_url`; `image_uploaded` still describes the stored source. Uploaded-image URLs return 404 with no-store while uploads are disabled. Re-enabling restores delivery. Third-party copies/caches of previously public images cannot be revoked. Startup seeds only missing settings, and old settings forms that omit this field preserve the existing policy.

Social platforms build link cards from the fetched page's Open Graph (`og:title`, `og:description`, `og:image`) and Twitter Card tags. Without custom preview settings, urlet keeps its redirect behavior and the platform may read metadata from the destination. Configured links serve metadata from the owner's saved preview fields to recognised social crawlers. The platform chooses the footer, layout and refresh timing; there is no arbitrary footer field in these tags.

These endpoints require the link owner's session or API token; another owner's link returns 404. Existing CSRF rules apply to cookie requests. Create a short link first, then configure its optional public preview. The public shortener does not accept uploads or these extra fields.

| Method | Path | Behavior |
|--------|------|----------|
| GET | `/api/v1/urls/{id}/preview` | Returns `{title, description, image_url, image_uploaded, enabled}`; an unconfigured preview returns null fields and false flags |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/urls/{id}/preview` | JSON `{title?, description?, image_url?}`. Omitted fields stay unchanged; null or blank clears the field. Setting/clearing image_url replaces/removes any uploaded image. The response uses the GET shape |
| POST | `/api/v1/urls/{id}/preview/image` | Multipart field `image`; replaces the image while preserving text, returns the GET shape |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/urls/{id}/preview` | Clears all custom preview data and image bytes, returns 204 |

```bash
curl -X PATCH "$BASE/api/v1/urls/42/preview" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Read this","description":"A custom summary","image_url":"https://example.com/card.png"}'
curl "$BASE/api/v1/urls/42/preview/image" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -F 'image=@card.png'
```

Title: 200 characters; description: 1000 characters. Image URLs must be absolute HTTPS, at most 2048 characters, without credentials/whitespace. Uploads: PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP, at most 2 MiB and 4096 × 4096 pixels. MIME is detected from validated bytes, not the filename. Stored images use opaque public `/assets/link-previews/{key}` URLs; replacing/removing the image revokes old keys. Invalid fields return 422; malformed/oversized multipart requests return a 4xx error without changing stored data. Uploads share a per-account rate budget.

Configured text/images are public even on password-protected links. A blank preview title uses the site name; private link title/notes and the destination are never used as fallbacks. No external metadata or image fetch occurs on the server. Known social crawlers (including Discord, X/Twitter, Meta, Telegram, Slack, LinkedIn and LINE markers) receive OG/Twitter HTML; unknown agents retain normal link behavior. Link lifecycle checks apply to both metadata and uploaded images. Custom preview fetches do not count as clicks. Third-party caches and layout are controlled by the platforms; changing settings does not guarantee an immediate refreshed card.

---

## Tags [#tags]

### `GET /api/v1/tags` [#get-apiv1tags]

`200` → `{ "items": [ { "id": 1, "name": "campaign", "color": null, "url_count": 4 } ] }`

### `DELETE /api/v1/tags/{id}` [#delete-apiv1tagsid]

`204`, deletes the tag (it only unlinks the tag from short links; the links themselves are
untouched).

---

## Public endpoints [#public-endpoints]

### `GET /` [#get-]

The landing page: an introduction to the service with sign-in and sign-up entry points. It no
longer redirects to `/app`; a visitor who is already signed in sees a button that opens the
dashboard.

When the visitor is allowed to create a link — see the `public_create_access` setting below — the
page also carries the public shortener. `?shortened=<slug>&domain=<hostname>` renders the short URL
of a link that was just created; the value is resolved against the database, so the result box never
prints a query-string value verbatim and never discloses the destination.

### `POST /` [#post-]

The public shortener form (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`), available on the canonical host
only. It accepts `target_url` (required) plus the optional inputs the administrator enabled:
`slug`, `title`, `tags` (comma separated), `password`, `expires_at`, `max_clicks`, `redirect_mode`,
`splash_delay_seconds`, `splash_title`, `splash_message`, `domain`, and the provider token field
(`cf-turnstile-response` or `g-recaptcha-response`).

A successful submission is `303` to `/?shortened=<slug>&domain=<hostname>`. A failure is `303` to
`/?err=<code>`, where `<code>` is one of `denied` (below the access level, or a disabled field),
`guest_allowlist` (anonymous destination not allowed), `rate_limited`, `captcha`, `quota` (the `public_max_urls` budget of the Guest account is full),
`conflict`, `slug`, `target`, `expiry`, `tags`, `password_rules`, `domain`, `mode_denied` or
`invalid`. A non-numeric `max_clicks` or `splash_delay_seconds` is reported as `invalid` rather
than silently dropped.

The CSRF same-origin rule applies to the form, and the ordinary security headers are unchanged.

### `POST /api/v1/public/urls` [#post-apiv1publicurls]

The same operation as JSON, for scripts. No credential is required when `public_create_access` is
`guest`; a session cookie or a Bearer token may be supplied instead, and the link is then owned by
that account.

Anonymous requests must also match the enabled guest destination allowlist; the example below is included in the built-in rules. Signed-in sessions and Bearer tokens use their existing account permissions.

```json
{
  "target_url": "https://github.com/cxyfer/urlet",
  "slug": "launch",
  "title": "Launch day",
  "captcha_token": "0.abc..."
}
```

`201`:

```json
{
  "domain": "s.example.com",
  "slug": "launch",
  "short_url": "https://s.example.com/launch",
  "target_url": "https://github.com/cxyfer/urlet",
  "created_at": "2026-10-22T12:00:00.000Z"
}
```

The link id is deliberately not returned: the caller has no account to manage the link with.

- `403` `forbidden` — the caller is below the access level, or submitted a field the administrator
  disabled, or an anonymous destination is not on the enabled guest allowlist
- `400` `captcha_failed` — the bot protection check failed (fail closed)
- `429` `rate_limited` — the per-address or the shared visitor budget is exhausted (`Retry-After`)
- `409` `conflict` — the requested slug is already taken
- `422` `validation_error` — an invalid target URL or option

### `GET /health` [#get-health]

```json
{ "status": "ok", "version": "1.4.0-rc.3", "database": "ok", "uptime_seconds": 42 }
```

When the database cannot be queried the response is `503` with `status` set to `degraded`.
`/healthz` is an alias of the same endpoint.

### `GET /{slug}` [#get-slug]

- Valid, unprotected and `redirect_mode = direct` → `30x` + `Location` (301/308 send
  `private, max-age=300`; 302/307 send `private, no-store`)
- Valid, unprotected and `redirect_mode = splash` → `200` splash page (`no-store`). It
  shows the custom copy, the destination host and a countdown, sends the visitor on with a
  `<meta http-equiv="refresh">` and also offers a "Continue now" link. The click is recorded when
  the splash page is served, not when the visitor leaves
- Password protected → `200` password prompt (**the target URL is never disclosed**). After a
  successful unlock the destination is served directly: the password page is the only
  interstitial, so a splash page is never shown for a protected link
- Expired or click limit reached → `410`
- Missing / deleted / disabled → `404`

### `POST /{slug}/unlock` [#post-slugunlock]

Accepts `application/json` or `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`:

```json
{ "password": "linkpass" }
```

- Successful JSON request → `200` `{ "ok": true, "redirect": "/slug" }` + unlock cookie
- Successful form request → `303` redirect to `/{slug}` + unlock cookie
- Wrong password → JSON `401`; forms re-render the password page (`401`)
- Rate limited → `429`

### `GET /api/v1/public/urls/{slug}?domain=<hostname>` [#get-apiv1publicurlsslugdomainhostname]

Public metadata without the target URL. Without `domain` the default domain is used, which keeps
callers that predate multi-domain working for links on the default domain.

```json
{ "domain": "go.example.com", "slug": "promo", "title": "Launch", "has_password": true, "redirect_mode": "splash", "is_expired": false, "state": "active" }
```

### `GET /api/v1/domains` [#get-apiv1domains]

Authenticated users can list the active domains available for new links, already filtered by
their group policy. `is_default` marks the effective group default:

```json
[ { "id": 1, "hostname": "s.example.com", "is_default": true }, { "id": 2, "hostname": "go.example.com", "is_default": false } ]
```

---

## Invite codes (member) [#invite-codes-member]

Members can issue invite codes for their **own group** when that group has
`allow_invites` enabled. Codes are pinned to the group, so anyone who redeems one
joins it. The group's calendar quota (`max_invites` / `invite_period`) applies and
is shared with administrator-issued codes. Revoking a code that nobody redeemed
returns its slot; a redeemed code keeps it.

### `GET /api/v1/invites` [#get-apiv1invites]

`GET /api/v1/invites?page=&per_page=` → `200`: the caller's own codes (newest
first), including the displayable code and its registration link, plus the
effective quota.

```json
{
  "items": [
    { "id": 4, "prefix": "RW6M", "code": "RW6MF6C6JG",
      "link": "https://s.example.com/app/register?invite=RW6MF6C6JG",
      "note": "team", "group_id": 4, "max_uses": 2,
      "used_count": 1, "remaining": 1, "expires_at": null, "status": "active",
      "usable": true, "created_at": "2026-03-18T10:00:00.000Z" }
  ],
  "page": 1, "per_page": 20, "total": 1,
  "quota": { "group_id": 4, "group_name": "Invite Team", "allowed": true,
             "limit": 5, "period": "month", "used": 1, "remaining": 4 }
}
```

`code` and `link` are `null` for codes created before sealed storage or after
`URLET_SECRET` changed; `prefix` is always present. `link` is also `null` when
the code is revoked, exhausted or expired, while `code` stays visible for
history. `per_page` defaults to 20 and
is capped at 100. `quota.allowed` is `false` when the group does not enable
member invites: creating a code then returns `403`, but codes issued before the
toggle was turned off remain listed and revocable. `remaining` is `null` when
`limit` is `0` (unlimited). Accounts whose group link is missing fall back to the
default group.

Member issuance is throttled to 20 codes per hour per account (`429` when the
burst is exhausted); the group's invite quota remains the primary limit. A group
with no finite quota is otherwise unlimited.

### `POST /api/v1/invites` [#post-apiv1invites]

`{ "note"?: "team", "max_uses"?: 2 }` → `201`:

```json
{ "code": "RW6MF6C6JG", "link": "https://s.example.com/app/register?invite=RW6MF6C6JG",
  "invite": { "...": "..." }, "quota": { "...": "..." } }
```

The code and link are also returned by `GET /api/v1/invites`, so they are not
lost when the response is dismissed. The top-level `link` mirrors `invite.link`;
both are `null` if the created code is already unusable. `max_uses` must be
between 1 and 10 for
member codes. `403` when the group does not allow invites or the period quota is
exhausted (`error.code = "forbidden"`), and `429` when the hourly burst limit is
exhausted.

### `DELETE /api/v1/invites/{id}` [#delete-apiv1invitesid]

`204`, revokes one of the caller's own codes. Another member's code is reported
as `404`; administrators use `DELETE /api/v1/admin/invites/{id}` for any code.
Revoking a code that nobody redeemed returns its quota slot; a code that was
already redeemed keeps it.

---

## Administration (requires `role = admin`) [#administration-requires-role--admin]

Every `/api/v1/admin/**` endpoint returns `403 forbidden` for non-administrators.

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/admin/users?q=&role=&status=&group_id=&page=&per_page=` | User list (includes `link_count`, `group_id`, `group_name`) |
| PATCH | `/admin/users/{id}` | `{ "role"?, "status"?, "display_name"?, "group_id"? }`; `group_id: null` makes the user ungrouped |
| POST | `/admin/users/{id}/password` | `{ "new_password": "..." }` → `204`, revokes every session for that account |
| DELETE | `/admin/users/{id}` | `204`, soft-deletes the account and all of its short links |
| GET | `/admin/domains` | Every domain with link counts, status and source |
| POST | `/admin/domains` | `{ "hostname": "go.example.com" }` → `201`, created as `pending` |
| PATCH | `/admin/domains/{id}` | `{ "status"?: "active"\|"disabled", "is_default"?: true }` |
| DELETE | `/admin/domains/{id}` | `204`; only a zero-link UI domain that is not the default |
| GET | `/admin/groups?page=&per_page=` | Group list with member counts (paginated) |
| POST | `/admin/groups` | `{ "name", "description"?, "max_urls"?, "max_api_tokens"?, "max_invites"?, "invite_period"?, "allow_invites"?, "allow_custom_slug"?, "allow_password"?, "allow_expiry"?, "allow_max_clicks"?, "allow_tags"?, "allow_api_tokens"?, "allow_domain_selection"?, "redirect_mode_policy"?, "default_domain_id"?, "restrict_domains"?, "domain_ids"?, "is_default"? }` → `201`; `default_domain_id` must reference an active domain; `domain_ids` must reference existing domains (disabled entries stay stored but are not selectable) |
| PUT | `/admin/groups/{id}` | `name` is required; other omitted fields keep their current value; `max_urls` / `max_api_tokens` / `max_invites` set to `null` inherit the site quota; `description: null` clears it; `redirect_mode_policy` is `direct`, `splash` or `choice` and is omitted to keep the current value; `default_domain_id: null` means the site default; `domain_ids: null` or `[]` clears the allowlist; `is_default: true` moves the single default marker |
| DELETE | `/admin/groups/{id}?reassign_to={id}` | `204`, moves the members then deletes; `409` for the default group or a missing/invalid target |
| GET | `/admin/themes` | Theme catalogue (key, name, description, `enabled`, `default`, `appearance`, `dark_only`, `light_only`, `css_url`, `custom`) plus `switching` (`all` or `admin`); includes administrator uploads |
| PUT | `/admin/themes` | `{ "enabled"?: ["verdant", ...], "default"?: "verdant", "switching"?: "all"\|"admin" }`; omitted fields keep their value; at least one enabled theme and an enabled default are required (`422` otherwise). `enabled` and `default` may name `custom-…` uploads |
| GET | `/admin/urls?q=&status=&user_id=&page=&sort=&per_page=` | Every short link on the instance; `sort` accepts the same values as `GET /api/v1/urls` |
| PATCH | `/admin/urls/{id}` | `{ "status"?, "redirect_type"? }` |
| DELETE | `/admin/urls/{id}` | `204` |
| GET | `/admin/invites` | The 200 newest invite codes with `code`, `link`, `prefix`, `group_id` / `group_name`; there is no pagination. `code` and `link` are `null` for legacy or secret-rotated rows, and `link` is also `null` for revoked, exhausted or expired codes |
| POST | `/admin/invites` | `{ "note"?, "max_uses"?, "expires_at"?, "group_id"? }` → `201` `{ "code", "link", "invite" }`; `link` mirrors `invite.link` and is `null` if the code is already unusable; the code stays available from `GET` and the link is returned while usable; `403` when the group's per-period invite quota is exhausted |
| DELETE | `/admin/invites/{id}` | `204`, revoke; an unused code returns its quota slot, a redeemed code keeps it |
| GET | `/admin/settings` | Current settings, including `theme_switching` (`all` or `admin`) |
| PUT | `/admin/settings` | `{ "site_name": "...", "registration_mode": "invite", "theme_switching": "admin", ... }` |
| GET | `/admin/audit?action=&target_type=&actor=&page=` | Audit log (`metadata` is parsed into JSON) |
| GET | `/admin/stats` | User / short link / click totals, database size, version, uptime |

Theme uploads are administrator-only browser multipart forms at `/app/admin/themes/custom` (create),
`/app/admin/themes/custom/{id}` (edit/replace CSS) and `/app/admin/themes/custom/{id}/delete`. The
JSON API deliberately has no file-upload endpoint. Uploads are CSS-only, at most 256 KiB, UTF-8;
absolute external references and cross-origin `url(...)` are rejected, with the CSP as the second
line of defence; see [`THEMES.md`](/en/docs/themes).

`GroupDto` also returns `default_domain_id`, `default_domain` (the stored value, even if the domain
is disabled), `restrict_domains`, `allowed_domain_ids` and `allowed_domains`, plus the invite
quota (`max_invites`, `invite_period`) and its live counters (`invites_used`,
`invites_remaining`; the latter is `null` when unlimited). The request field is
`domain_ids` (`null` or `[]` clears it; omitting keeps it); the response uses `allowed_*`. `GET /api/v1/auth/me` returns the *effective* fallback
default, which can differ from `default_domain` when the stored group default is disabled.

**User groups.** A group object is
`{ id, name, description, max_urls, max_api_tokens, max_invites, invite_period, allow_*,
is_default, members, created_at, updated_at }`. `redirect_mode_policy` is `direct`, `splash` or
`choice` (create default `choice`). `allow_invites` is opt-in (`false` on create) and
lets the group's members issue their own codes, drawn from the same quota as administrator-issued
codes.
Quotas are nullable: `null` inherits the site-wide setting, `0` means unlimited. Feature toggles
default to `true`; they gate new uses and never alter existing links or tokens. Administrators
follow the same rules as other users. `PUT` accepts a partial group: omitted fields keep their
current value, quotas set to `null` inherit the site quota, `description: null` clears it, and
`is_default: true` moves the marker. `POST` keeps the create defaults (omitted toggles are allowed,
omitted quotas inherit).

**Invite quotas.** Each group may issue a limited number of invite codes per calendar period.
`max_invites` is nullable (`null` inherits the site-wide `max_invites_per_period`, `0` is
unlimited) and `invite_period` is `day`, `week` (Monday start) or `month`, evaluated in UTC.
Issuing past the limit returns `403` with `error.code = "forbidden"` and a message naming the
limit. The counter lives in an issuance ledger: revoking a code that nobody redeemed releases its
slot, while a redeemed code keeps it. The quota resets by itself at the next period boundary.
Upgrading releases codes that were already revoked and never redeemed, so the counter can drop once.
Invites created without `group_id` consume the site-wide quota instead.

**Guard rails**: an administrator cannot change their own role or status, cannot delete
themselves, and the instance always keeps at least one active administrator (otherwise the
request fails with `409`). The default group cannot be deleted; move the marker with `PUT` first.

Editable setting keys: `site_name`, `registration_mode` (`open`/`invite`/`closed`),
`default_slug_length` (4–16), `max_urls_per_user` (0 = unlimited),
`max_api_tokens_per_user` (0 = unlimited, default 20),
`max_invites_per_period` (0 = unlimited, default 0), `invite_period` (`day`/`week`/`month`,
default `month`), `default_redirect_type` (301/302/307/308), `analytics_enabled`,
`theme_switching` (`all`/`admin`, default `all`),
`preview_image_policy` (`none`/`url`/`upload`/`both`, default `both`),
`click_retention_days` (0 = keep forever), plus the bot verification keys
`captcha_provider`, `captcha_site_key`, `captcha_secret_key`, `captcha_on_register`,
`captcha_on_login`, `captcha_on_create` and `captcha_allowed_hostnames`. The secret key is
write-only: it is never returned in plaintext, and submitting it empty keeps the stored value.

The public shortener adds `public_create_access` (`guest`/`user`/`admin`, default `user`),
`public_captcha` (default `true`), `public_rate_limit_per_ip` (guest creations per period, default 20,
`0` = unlimited), `public_rate_limit_per_ip_period` (default `hour`), `public_rate_limit_global`
(shared guest creations per period, default 500, `0` = unlimited),
`public_rate_limit_global_period` (default `hour`), `public_max_urls` (total links the reserved Guest account may own, default 1000, `0` =
unlimited; separate from `max_urls_per_user`) and the field switches `public_allow_slug`, `public_allow_title` (both default `true`)
plus `public_allow_tags`, `public_allow_password`, `public_allow_expiry`, `public_allow_max_clicks`,
`public_allow_redirect` and `public_allow_domain` (all default `false`).

Guest quota periods accept `minute`, `hour`, `day`, `week` or `month`. They use the server process timezone (`TZ`, otherwise the OS timezone); Docker Compose defaults `TZ` to `UTC`, and operators can set `TZ=Asia/Taipei`, for example. The admin page shows the timezone and reveals guest rate, total-link, captcha and destination allowlist settings only when `public_create_access=guest`. Hidden settings are preserved; without JavaScript, save the access level to reveal the fields. Public-form field switches remain visible because they also apply to signed-in callers.

The guest destination policy adds two string settings:

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `guest_allowlist_enabled` | `"true"` | Restrict only anonymous creation; `"false"` explicitly disables the policy |
| `guest_allowlist` | Built-in known-site rules | One ASCII hostname per line, optionally with a leading `*.` and a case-sensitive ASCII path, for example `*.example.com/articles/` |

Use `PUT /api/v1/admin/settings` to edit either key. Hostnames are lowercased, blank lines and duplicates removed. Only a leading `*.` wildcard is accepted; no scheme, port, credentials, other wildcard, query, fragment, encoded rule path or dot segment is accepted. A bare host allows any path; `/articles` allows that path and its descendants, while `/articles/` requires the trailing slash. Query strings and fragments do not contribute to a match. Target paths with encoded separators or nested encoding are refused for path-scoped rules. Only HTTP/HTTPS with their standard ports are allowed. Without `*.`, hostnames match exactly. `*.example.com` matches `a.example.com` and `a.b.example.com` at DNS label boundaries, but excludes `example.com`, `evilexample.com` and `example.com.evil.test`. List `example.com` separately to include the root. The limits are 200 rules and 16 KiB; invalid edits return `422` and leave the entire settings batch unchanged.

An enabled empty list denies all anonymous destinations. Disabling the policy preserves its list. Updates take effect immediately and persist across restarts; upgrades seed only missing keys. Existing guest links continue to redirect. The admin form offers the same controls and preserves these settings when an older form omits them. Visitors can inspect the current allowed destinations on the landing page; refused forms use `?err=guest_allowlist`.

The built-in list has 43 host rules across 24 established services. These entries allow all paths on the listed hosts; administrators can still add optional path restrictions to their own rules. Root domains and subdomains are listed separately where needed. The default scope is:

| Area | Services and allowed hosts |
|------|----------------------------|
| Knowledge and development | Wikipedia (`wikipedia.org`, `*.wikipedia.org`), GitHub (`github.com`), GitLab (`gitlab.com`), Stack Overflow (`stackoverflow.com`, `*.stackoverflow.com`), Stack Exchange (`stackexchange.com`, `*.stackexchange.com`), MDN (`developer.mozilla.org`), Python documentation (`docs.python.org`), Rust documentation (`doc.rust-lang.org`) |
| Taiwan discussion | PTT (`ptt.cc`, `www.ptt.cc`), Dcard (`dcard.tw`, `www.dcard.tw`), Bahamut (`gamer.com.tw`, `*.gamer.com.tw`) |
| Video and music | YouTube (`*.youtube.com`, `youtube.com`), Bilibili (`bilibili.com`, `*.bilibili.com`), Twitch (`twitch.tv`, `*.twitch.tv`), Spotify (`spotify.com`, `*.spotify.com`) |
| Social | Reddit (`reddit.com`, `*.reddit.com`), Instagram (`instagram.com`, `www.instagram.com`), Facebook (`facebook.com`, `*.facebook.com`), X (`x.com`, `www.x.com`) |
| News | CNA (`cna.com.tw`, `www.cna.com.tw`), BBC (`bbc.com`, `www.bbc.com`, `bbc.co.uk`, `www.bbc.co.uk`), Reuters (`reuters.com`, `www.reuters.com`) |
| Product support | Apple (`support.apple.com`), Microsoft (`support.microsoft.com`) |

Public website hosting domains such as `*.github.io`, `*.gitlab.io` and `sites.google.com` are not included. GitHub and GitLab document that users can publish their own sites on their Pages domains; allowing the main service does not imply allowing those separate hosting domains. See the official [GitHub Pages](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/what-is-github-pages) and [GitLab Pages](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/pages/) documentation. This is a starting policy, not a safety certification: known hosts can carry user content or redirects. There is no reputation API, target fetch or redirect-chain inspection.

---

### Tracking parameter cleanup [#tracking-parameter-cleanup]

Administrators can enable cleanup under **Admin → Settings** or with `PUT /api/v1/admin/settings`:

```json
{
  "url_cleaning_enabled": "true",
  "url_cleaning_rules": "example.com utm_* ref\nexample.org campaign_id"
}
```

Both settings are returned by `GET /api/v1/admin/settings`; defaults are `"false"` and `""`. Setting values are strings, as with all other settings. Only administrators may read or change them. Invalid settings return `422`; a rejected batch changes neither the database nor the settings cache.

Each rule is `hostname parameter [parameter ...]`, one per line. It matches the named host and its subdomains, ignoring ASCII case in hostnames and decoded parameter names. A final `*` on a nonempty parameter name matches a prefix. Blank lines and whole-line `#` comments are ignored. Limits: 8192 bytes total, 100 rules, 32 parameters per rule and 64 bytes per parameter (including `*`). Domains must be ASCII hostnames with at least two nonempty labels, at most 253 bytes total and 63 bytes per label; labels use letters, digits or hyphens and cannot start/end with a hyphen. Schemes, ports, paths, userinfo and wildcard domains are rejected. Parameters use letters, digits, `_`, `-` or `.`, optionally followed by one final `*`; bare `*` and regex are rejected.

Built-in rules cover Facebook (`facebook.com`), Instagram, Threads (`threads.net`, `threads.com`), X/Twitter, YouTube (`youtube.com`, `youtu.be`), TikTok and Bilibili, including subdomains. They remove `utm_*` plus explicit platform tracking parameters, including `fbclid`, `igsh`, YouTube's `si` and Bilibili's `spm_id_from`; video IDs, playlists and playback times are kept. The complete list is visible in the administrator settings page. Custom rules add to built-ins; an empty custom setting keeps only built-ins. Unknown domains remain untouched unless a custom rule matches them. Custom rules can change meaningful content if they remove required parameters.

Cleanup applies **only when creating links**, through `POST /api/v1/urls`, `POST /api/v1/public/urls`, the dashboard and the public form. For example, `https://youtu.be/ABC?si=tracking&t=90` is stored and returned as `https://youtu.be/ABC?t=90`. The original target must pass validation before cleanup. Kept query components retain their original encoding, values and order; fragments remain intact. Share shortlinks are not expanded and targets are never fetched. Existing links, target edits and redirects are unchanged. Disabling cleanup preserves custom rules for later use.

---

## Audit action codes [#audit-action-codes]

| Action | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `auth.register` / `auth.login` / `auth.login_failed` / `auth.logout` | Authentication events |
| `auth.password_changed` / `auth.session_revoked` / `user.profile_updated` | Account changes |
| `url.created` / `url.updated` / `url.deleted` | Short link changes |
| `token.created` / `token.revoked` | API tokens |
| `invite.created` / `invite.revoked` / `invite.redeemed` | Invite codes |
| `domain.created` / `domain.updated` / `domain.deleted` / `domain.default_changed` | Domain administration |
| `admin.user_updated` / `admin.user_deleted` / `admin.password_reset` | Administrative actions |
| `admin.group_created` / `admin.group_updated` / `admin.group_deleted` | Group changes |
| `admin.url_updated` / `admin.settings_updated` / `admin.themes_updated` / `admin.theme_created` / `admin.theme_updated` / `admin.theme_deleted` | Administrative actions |

---

## Rate limits [#rate-limits]

| Scope | Limit |
|-------|-------|
| Login | 10 attempts per 5 minutes per (IP, email), **and** 40 per 5 minutes per IP (across accounts) |
| Registration | 5 attempts per hour per IP |
| Short link unlock | 10 attempts per 5 minutes per (slug, IP) |
| Short link creation | 120 per hour per user |
| Public shortener | Anonymous visitors only: `public_rate_limit_per_ip` per `public_rate_limit_per_ip_period` and `public_rate_limit_global` per `public_rate_limit_global_period` (defaults: 20/hour and 500/hour). Periods are calendar minute/hour/day/week/month in the server timezone, with Monday-based weeks and actual calendar months. `0` disables either budget. The per-address budget is charged before bot protection, the shared one only after success. SQLite counters survive restart; `Retry-After` is the time to the next boundary. Signed-in callers retain group quotas and the existing per-account throttle, without consuming guest quotas |
| Password change | 10 per hour per user |

The persistent guest-quota table holds at most 50,000 rows across sources, shared budgets and periods. At capacity, new rows return `429`; existing counters keep their usage and limits. Reservations reclaim expired windows immediately, and maintenance also cleans them. Active counters are never evicted to make room for new addresses.

Exceeding a limit returns `429` with `Retry-After` (seconds). The in-memory counters reset on
restart, but **account lockout** is persistent: once one email accumulates 30 failures within
15 minutes, even the correct password returns `429` (`Retry-After: 900`) until the window slides
past.

The IP used for login comes from `X-Real-IP` when `URLET_TRUST_PROXY=true`, falling back to the
rightmost address in `X-Forwarded-For`.

---

## UI language [#ui-language]

The web UI ships in English (`en`), Traditional Chinese (`zh-Hant`) and Simplified Chinese
(`zh-Hans`). On a first visit the language is chosen from the browser's `Accept-Language`
header; when nothing matches, English is used. The selection is stored in the `urlet_lang`
cookie.

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/app/lang/{code}?next=<path>` | Switch the UI language, set the `urlet_lang` cookie, then return `302` to `next` (or to `/app` when `next` is missing or not a same-site relative path) |

`code` is one of `en`, `zh-Hant`, `zh-Hans`; `next` must be a same-site relative path.
An unrecognized `code` falls back to English (it is never an error), and a visitor without a
cookie is negotiated from `Accept-Language` instead — a present cookie always wins.

The language setting only affects rendered HTML. **JSON responses are always English** and
never change with the selected language.

---

## Bot verification [#bot-verification]

urlet can require a CAPTCHA on the three public forms that create state: the web registration
form, the web sign-in form, and the web create-short-link form. The JSON API endpoints
`POST /api/v1/auth/register` and `POST /api/v1/auth/login` accept the widget token in the optional
`captcha_token` field. It is off by default and configured either through environment variables or
in the admin UI under **Admin → Settings**; a non-empty environment variable overrides the admin
setting. See the deployment guide for the variables and for how to obtain provider keys.

| Provider | `provider` value | Widget |
|----------|------------------|--------|
| Disabled (default) | `none` | None |
| Cloudflare Turnstile | `turnstile` | Managed Turnstile widget |
| Google reCAPTCHA v2 | `recaptcha` | "I'm not a robot" checkbox |

Verification applies to a form only when all four conditions hold: the provider is not `none`,
the site key is non-empty, the secret key is non-empty, and the matching per-form switch
(`captcha_on_register`, `captcha_on_login` or `captcha_on_create`) is `true`.

Failure is **closed**: a missing, malformed, expired or already-used token — including a timeout
or any non-2xx response from the provider — rejects the submission.

The `hostname` reported by the provider is also checked: it must equal the host of the instance's
base URL or one of the extra hostnames in `captcha_allowed_hostnames` (comma-separated, up to 10).
A response whose `hostname` is missing or empty is accepted, and a mismatch is rejected and logged
at `WARN`.

| Surface | Verification |
|---------|--------------|
| Web registration form (`POST /app/register`) | Applies when enabled for registration |
| Web sign-in form (`POST /app/login`) | Applies when enabled for sign-in |
| Web create-short-link form (`POST /app/urls`) | Applies when enabled for link creation |
| `POST /api/v1/auth/register` | Applies when enabled for registration; send the widget token in `captcha_token`; failure returns `400` with `error.code = "captcha_failed"` |
| `POST /api/v1/auth/login` | Applies when enabled for sign-in; send the widget token in `captcha_token`; failure returns `400` with `error.code = "captcha_failed"` |
| `POST /api/v1/urls` | **API tokens only** — exempt when the request carries `Authorization: Bearer ur_...`; a session-cookie call is subject to the link-creation switch and takes an optional `captcha_token` |


# urlet deployment guide (/en/docs/deployment)

## 1. Requirements [#1-requirements]

| Item | Minimum | Recommended |
|------|---------|-------------|
| CPU | 1 vCPU | 2 vCPU |
| Memory | 128 MB | 256 MB |
| Disk | 100 MB + data | 1 GB |
| Docker | 24.x | Latest |
| Docker Compose | 2.24 (`!override` / `!reset` are used by the overlays) | Latest |

No external database, Redis or reverse proxy is needed. A single container can serve traffic on
its own (putting a TLS terminator in front of it is recommended).

## 2. Quick start (HTTP) [#2-quick-start-http]

```bash
git clone https://github.com/cxyfer/urlet urlet && cd urlet
cp .env.example .env
```

Edit `.env`:

```ini
URLET_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080      # public URL; use https:// once TLS is in front (§3)
URLET_PORT=8080                            # host port to publish (read by docker compose only)
URLET_ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@example.com
URLET_ADMIN_PASSWORD=<strong password>
URLET_REGISTRATION=invite                  # optional: open / invite / closed
```

> Keep the scheme of `URLET_BASE_URL` in step with how visitors actually reach the instance: an
> `https://` value makes urlet mark the session cookie `Secure`, so serving plain HTTP while
> `URLET_BASE_URL` says `https://` signs users out again immediately (§4, §12).

Start it:

```bash
docker compose up -d --build
docker compose logs -f urlet
```

Verify:

```bash
curl -fsS http://localhost:8080/health
docker compose exec urlet /usr/local/bin/urlet healthcheck
```

### 2.1 Prebuilt image [#21-prebuilt-image]

Every `v*` tag publishes a multi-arch image (`linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`) to GHCR. To run a
published release instead of building locally:

```bash
export URLET_IMAGE=ghcr.io/cxyfer/urlet:v1.3.0   # pin the release you want
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.image.yml up -d
```

- `URLET_IMAGE` defaults to `ghcr.io/cxyfer/urlet:latest`; pin an exact version in production
  rather than tracking `latest`. When you do use `latest`, run `docker compose -f
  docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.image.yml pull` before `up -d` to fetch a newer release.
- The overlay removes the `build` section, so compose pulls the image and never falls back to a
  local Rust build.
- The package defaults to **private**. Either authenticate (`docker login ghcr.io` with a token
  that has `read:packages`) or make the package public under *Package settings → Change
  visibility*.
- The image runs as uid/gid `10001`, exactly like a locally built one, so the `/data` volume
  permissions are unchanged.

## 3. Automatic HTTPS (Caddy) [#3-automatic-https-caddy]

```bash
export URLET_DOMAIN=s.example.com
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.tls.yml up -d --build
```

- Point the A/AAAA record for `s.example.com` at this host first; Caddy obtains and renews the
  certificate automatically.
- The overlay stops publishing the urlet port (it is only reachable inside the compose network)
  and sets `URLET_BASE_URL`, `URLET_SECURE_COOKIES=true` and `URLET_TRUST_PROXY=true` for you.
- Certificates live in the `urlet-caddy-data` volume.

If you already run Nginx or Traefik, reverse proxy to `127.0.0.1:8080` yourself and set:

```ini
URLET_BASE_URL=https://s.example.com
URLET_SECURE_COOKIES=true
URLET_TRUST_PROXY=true      # only when you are sure the proxy overwrites X-Forwarded-*
```

## 4. Configuration reference [#4-configuration-reference]

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `URLET_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8080` | Public URL; used to build short links, for the CSRF same-origin check and to decide whether cookies are `Secure`. The host must be ASCII (punycode for IDN); IPv6 literals and underscore service names are accepted for the canonical host only |
| `URLET_DOMAINS` | Empty | Extra redirect-only hostnames, comma separated. Inserted as active on first boot; never overrides an existing status. Every domain must use the same http/https scheme as `URLET_BASE_URL` and needs DNS + TLS |
| `URLET_BIND` | `0.0.0.0:8080` | Listen address |
| `URLET_DATABASE_URL` | `sqlite:///data/urlet.db?mode=rwc` | SQLite connection string |
| `URLET_DATA_DIR` | Directory holding the database | Where the auto-generated secret is written |
| `URLET_THEMES_DIR` | `<URLET_DATA_DIR>/themes` | Where uploaded theme stylesheets are stored. docker compose mounts the `urlet-themes` volume at `/data/themes` |
| `URLET_SECRET` | Auto-generated | HMAC secret (at least 16 characters, 32+ recommended; the generated one is 44 characters of base64); **changing it invalidates every session and unlock cookie and makes existing invite codes unreadable, though they still redeem** |
| `URLET_ADMIN_EMAIL` / `URLET_ADMIN_PASSWORD` | — | Create or promote the administrator at startup |
| `URLET_REGISTRATION` | Read from the settings table | Override the registration mode: `open` / `invite` / `closed`. `invite_only` is accepted as `invite` and `disabled`/`none` as `closed`; an unrecognised value falls back to `open` |
| `URLET_SECURE_COOKIES` | Derived from `BASE_URL` | Force the `Secure` cookie flag. The compose files always pass a value through (default `false`), so in Docker set it to `true` explicitly when you terminate TLS yourself; the TLS overlay does that for you |
| `URLET_TRUST_PROXY` | `false` | Trust `X-Forwarded-For` / `X-Forwarded-Proto` |
| `URLET_SESSION_TTL_HOURS` | `168` | Session lifetime |
| `URLET_UNLOCK_TTL_MINUTES` | `30` | Lifetime of the short link unlock cookie |
| `URLET_DEFAULT_SLUG_LENGTH` | Read from the settings table | Override the generated slug length (4–16) |
| `URLET_CAPTCHA_PROVIDER` | `none` | Bot verification provider: `none` / `turnstile` / `recaptcha` |
| `URLET_CAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` | Empty | Public site key rendered into the widget |
| `URLET_CAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` | Empty | Secret key used for server-side verification (server only; the admin UI never echoes it back) |
| `URLET_CAPTCHA_ON_REGISTER` | `false` | Apply bot verification to the registration form |
| `URLET_CAPTCHA_ON_LOGIN` | `false` | Apply bot verification to the sign-in form |
| `URLET_CAPTCHA_ON_CREATE` | `false` | Apply bot verification to the create-short-link form |
| `URLET_CAPTCHA_ALLOWED_HOSTNAMES` | Empty | Extra hostnames accepted in the provider's `hostname` response, comma-separated (up to 10); the host of `URLET_BASE_URL` is always accepted |
| `URLET_LOG` | `info` | tracing filter, for example `urlet=debug,tower=warn`. `RUST_LOG`, when set, takes precedence (the binary tries `EnvFilter::try_from_default_env` first) |
| `URLET_LOG_FORMAT` | `compact` | `compact` or `json` |
| `URLET_HEALTHCHECK_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/health` | Target of `urlet healthcheck` |
| `TZ` | OS timezone (`UTC` in the image) | Server process timezone for guest calendar quotas, for example `Asia/Taipei`; read at startup. Docker Compose forwards it (`TZ: ${TZ:-UTC}`) |

Three further variables are read by the compose files, not by the urlet binary:

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `URLET_PORT` | `8080` | Host port that `docker-compose.yml` publishes (the container itself always listens on 8080) |
| `URLET_DOMAIN` | — | Domain the `docker-compose.tls.yml` overlay requests a certificate for; required by that overlay |
| `URLET_IMAGE` | `ghcr.io/cxyfer/urlet:latest` | Image used by the `docker-compose.image.yml` overlay (ignored without it) |

Instance-level settings (site name, registration mode, quota, default redirect type, analytics
switch, click retention) are edited in **Admin → Settings**; they are stored in the database and
take effect immediately. A non-empty environment variable always overrides the value stored
there.

## 5. Multi-domain deployments [#5-multi-domain-deployments]

> **Upgrading from 1.2 or older:** back up the SQLite database first. The multi-domain migration
> (`0003_multi_domain`) rebuilds the `urls` table so the slug namespace becomes per domain; the
> migration is tested to preserve clicks, tags and daily stats, but a backup is the only rollback.

The canonical host keeps the application (`/`, `/app`, `/api/v1`). Extra domains are
redirect-only: `/{slug}` and `/{slug}/unlock` work, `/` renders the theme-aware short landing page
with the site tools, `/app` is redirected to the canonical host and `/api` returns 404. Each
domain has its own slug namespace. The full design is in [`MULTI_DOMAIN.md`](/en/docs/multi-domain).

- Seed extra domains with `URLET_DOMAINS=go.example.com,links.example.com`, or add them from
  `/app/admin/domains`.
- Domains added in the admin UI start as `pending`. Point DNS at this instance, add the hostname
  to the Caddy site label (or your reverse proxy), verify `https://<domain>/health`, then press
  **Activate**.
- The canonical domain cannot be disabled or deleted. The current default domain must be replaced
  before it can be disabled or deleted. If `URLET_BASE_URL` changes, the previous canonical domain
  is demoted to ordinary admin management on the next boot (its links keep working) and the default
  moves to the new canonical domain when the old one held it.
- All domains must use the same scheme as `URLET_BASE_URL`; do not mix http and https domains.
- The reverse proxy must preserve the original `Host` header. `X-Forwarded-Host` is not trusted in
  this version.
- `URLET_DOMAINS` is insert-only: disabling a seeded domain in the UI survives a restart. When the
  variable is set, removing a hostname from it detaches that domain to ordinary admin management on
  the next boot (status, links and default are preserved); it is not deleted automatically.
  Docker Compose always passes the variable, so an empty `URLET_DOMAINS` is treated as an explicit
  empty list.

## 6. Bot verification (CAPTCHA) [#6-bot-verification-captcha]

urlet can require a CAPTCHA on the three public forms that create state: the web registration
form, the web sign-in form, and the web create-short-link form. The JSON API endpoints
`POST /api/v1/auth/register` and `POST /api/v1/auth/login` are covered as well; they take the
widget token in the optional `captcha_token` field. `POST /api/v1/urls` is covered too, but only
for session-cookie calls (the link-creation switch); a call carrying
`Authorization: Bearer ur_...` stays exempt, so automation keeps working. Verification is disabled
by default.

### Supported providers [#supported-providers]

| Provider | Value | Notes |
|----------|-------|-------|
| Disabled | `none` | Default. No widget is rendered and nothing is verified |
| Cloudflare Turnstile | `turnstile` | Privacy-friendly, free tier, usually invisible to the visitor |
| Google reCAPTCHA v2 | `recaptcha` | The "I'm not a robot" checkbox |

### Variables [#variables]

All seven `URLET_CAPTCHA_*` variables are listed in the [configuration reference](#4-configuration-reference).
The shipped `docker-compose.yml` passes every one of them through, so setting them in `.env` is
enough — no compose edit is needed.

Verification becomes active for a form only when **all four** conditions hold: the provider is
not `none`, the site key is non-empty, the secret key is non-empty, and the matching `ON_*`
switch (`URLET_CAPTCHA_ON_REGISTER`, `URLET_CAPTCHA_ON_LOGIN` or `URLET_CAPTCHA_ON_CREATE`) is
`true`. Setting a provider without keys, or keys without a provider, silently leaves verification
off.

Failure is **closed**: a missing, malformed, expired or already-used token — including a timeout
or any non-2xx response from the provider — rejects the submission. On the web forms the visitor
sees a validation error; `POST /api/v1/auth/register`, `POST /api/v1/auth/login` and a
session-cookie `POST /api/v1/urls` return `400` with `error.code = "captcha_failed"` when the
matching switch is enabled.

### Token hostname (deployments with several hostnames) [#token-hostname-deployments-with-several-hostnames]

Both providers report the hostname the token was solved on in the `siteverify` response, and
urlet verifies it: the token must have been solved **on this instance**. The reported hostname
must therefore equal the host of `URLET_BASE_URL`, or one of the extra hostnames listed in
`URLET_CAPTCHA_ALLOWED_HOSTNAMES`. A response whose `hostname` is missing or empty is accepted —
not every provider or widget configuration returns the field.

`URLET_CAPTCHA_ALLOWED_HOSTNAMES` takes a comma-separated list of bare hostnames: each item is
trimmed and lowercased, empty items are dropped, and at most **10** items of 1–253 characters are
kept. Entries must not contain whitespace, `/`, `:` or `@`. Leaving it empty means "only the host
of `URLET_BASE_URL`", which is the right setting for the common single-domain deployment.

> **If your instance serves the forms on more than one hostname** (for example a short-link domain
> and a separate application domain, or an extra alias), list every one of those hostnames here.
> Tokens solved on a hostname that is neither the `URLET_BASE_URL` host nor on the list are
> rejected, which shows up as "the visitor solves the CAPTCHA but still cannot register or sign
> in". On a mismatch urlet logs a `WARN` line containing the reported hostname and the list of
> accepted candidates, which is the fastest way to find the missing entry.

### Getting the keys [#getting-the-keys]

**Cloudflare Turnstile**

1. Sign in to the Cloudflare dashboard and open **Turnstile**.
2. Choose **Add widget**, name it, and add the hostname(s) visitors will use to reach urlet
   (for example `s.example.com`; add `localhost` as well if you want to test locally).
3. Pick a widget mode (Managed is a good default) and create the widget.
4. Copy the **Site Key** and the **Secret Key**.

**Google reCAPTCHA v2**

1. Open the reCAPTCHA admin console and register a new site.
2. Select **reCAPTCHA v2** → **"I'm not a robot" Checkbox**.
3. Add the domain(s) of your instance.
4. Copy the **Site key** and the **Secret key**.

### Configuring it [#configuring-it]

In `.env` (docker compose):

```ini
URLET_CAPTCHA_PROVIDER=turnstile
URLET_CAPTCHA_SITE_KEY=0x4AAAAAAA...
URLET_CAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY=0x4AAAAAAA...
URLET_CAPTCHA_ON_REGISTER=true
URLET_CAPTCHA_ON_LOGIN=true
URLET_CAPTCHA_ON_CREATE=true
# Optional: extra hostnames whose tokens are accepted (comma-separated)
# URLET_CAPTCHA_ALLOWED_HOSTNAMES=www.example.com,alt.example.com
```

Then `docker compose up -d` to recreate the container.

The same values can be entered in the admin UI under **Admin → Settings**, which takes effect
without a restart. The secret key is write-only there: the stored value is never displayed, and
leaving the field blank keeps it as it is. Remember that a non-empty environment variable wins
over the admin setting, so configure each value in exactly one place.

### `remoteip` behind a reverse proxy [#remoteip-behind-a-reverse-proxy]

Server-side verification sends the visitor's IP address as `remoteip` so the provider can score
the request. urlet resolves that address exactly like the rate limiter does:

- `URLET_TRUST_PROXY=false` (the default) — the address is the direct peer, which is the proxy
  itself when one sits in front of urlet. Every visitor then looks like the same client to the
  provider, and only the token's own signals are used for scoring.
- `URLET_TRUST_PROXY=true` — `X-Real-IP` is preferred, falling back to the rightmost entry of
  `X-Forwarded-For`. The shipped `deploy/Caddyfile` sets
  `header_up X-Real-IP {remote_host}`, so Caddy passes the real visitor address.
- When no address can be determined, `remoteip` is omitted; both provider APIs treat it as
  optional, so verification still works.

Only enable `URLET_TRUST_PROXY` when the proxy is guaranteed to overwrite `X-Real-IP` /
`X-Forwarded-For`; otherwise a client can forge its address and also evade the rate limits.

## 7. Data and backups [#7-data-and-backups]

All state lives in `/data`: the `urlet-data` volume holds the database and secret, and the
`urlet-themes` volume (mounted at `/data/themes`) holds uploaded theme stylesheets:

```
/data/urlet.db          # main database
/data/urlet.db-wal      # write-ahead log
/data/urlet.db-shm
/data/secret.key         # auto-generated secret when URLET_SECRET is unset (0600)
/data/themes/*.css       # uploaded themes (urlet-themes volume)
```

### Backup [#backup]

SQLite runs in WAL mode, so copying the main file on its own can miss transactions that are still
in the WAL. Two safe approaches:

**Option A (host has `sqlite3`, no downtime)**

```bash
VOL=$(docker volume inspect -f '{{ .Mountpoint }}' urlet-data)
sudo sqlite3 "$VOL/urlet.db" ".backup '/tmp/urlet-$(date +%F).db'"
mv /tmp/urlet-$(date +%F).db ./backups/
```

`.backup` uses the SQLite online backup API and produces a consistent snapshot.

**Option B (no `sqlite3`)**

```bash
docker compose stop urlet          # a clean shutdown checkpoints the WAL
docker run --rm -v urlet-data:/data -v "$PWD":/backup alpine \
  cp /data/urlet.db "/backup/urlet-$(date +%F).db"
docker compose start urlet
```

Do not forget `secret.key`: if you rely on the auto-generated secret, back it up (or switch to the
`URLET_SECRET` environment variable), otherwise every session and unlock cookie is invalidated
after a restore and existing invite codes can no longer be displayed (they still redeem). A
data-directory backup contains both the database and that key, and invite codes are low-entropy, so
treat the whole backup as sensitive.

Uploaded themes are split across two volumes: the database holds the catalogue row and metadata,
while the CSS files live in `urlet-themes`. Back up both, otherwise a restore lists themes whose
stylesheets return 404. For example:

```bash
docker run --rm -v urlet-themes:/themes -v "$PWD":/backup alpine \
  tar -czf "/backup/urlet-themes-$(date +%F).tar.gz" -C /themes .
```

Restore them with the same helper and fix ownership (`chown -R 10001:10001`).

### Restore [#restore]

```bash
docker compose down
docker run --rm -v urlet-data:/data -v "$PWD":/backup alpine \
  sh -c 'rm -f /data/urlet.db*; cp /backup/urlet-YYYY-MM-DD.db /data/urlet.db; chown 10001:10001 /data/urlet.db'
docker run --rm -v urlet-themes:/themes -v "$PWD":/backup alpine \
  sh -c 'rm -rf /themes/*; tar -xzf /backup/urlet-themes-YYYY-MM-DD.tar.gz -C /themes; chown -R 10001:10001 /themes'
docker compose up -d
```

## 8. Upgrading [#8-upgrading]

```bash
git pull
docker compose up -d --build      # migrations are applied at startup
```

With a prebuilt image, change `URLET_IMAGE` to the new version and recreate the container:

```bash
export URLET_IMAGE=ghcr.io/cxyfer/urlet:v1.3.0
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.image.yml up -d
```

Migrations are forward-only additive files (`migrations/`), and applied files are checksum
protected: editing one makes startup fail instead of silently diverging. Back up before
upgrading.

## 9. Storage and disk usage [#9-storage-and-disk-usage]

| Data | Growth |
|------|--------|
| `urls` | About 300 bytes per row |
| `clicks` | About 150 bytes per row (can be pruned with `click_retention_days`) |
| `url_daily_stats` | One row per short link per day |
| `audit_logs` | About 200 bytes per row, retained for 180 days |
| `sessions` | Removed within a day of expiring or being revoked |
| `login_attempts` | Retained for 30 days |

100,000 clicks take roughly 15 MB. If you never prune, set `click_retention_days`.

## 10. Reverse proxy notes [#10-reverse-proxy-notes]

- Always set `URLET_BASE_URL` to the URL users actually see, otherwise short links point at the
  wrong domain.
- Only enable `URLET_TRUST_PROXY` when the proxy is **guaranteed to overwrite**
  `X-Forwarded-For` / `X-Real-IP`; otherwise clients can forge their IP and bypass the rate
  limits. The application prefers `X-Real-IP` (set by the proxy itself) and otherwise takes the
  rightmost entry of `X-Forwarded-For`, so appending proxies are safe too. The shipped
  `deploy/Caddyfile` already sets `header_up X-Real-IP {remote_host}`.
- `Host`, `X-Forwarded-For` and `X-Forwarded-Proto` must be forwarded; Caddy handles this
  automatically.
- Invite links carry the code in `?invite=`; reverse-proxy access logs that record query strings
  expose it. Restrict or redact those logs, or share the code instead.

## 11. Monitoring [#11-monitoring]

- Health check: `GET /health` (200 = healthy, 503 = database problem)
- The container ships a `HEALTHCHECK` that runs `urlet healthcheck` (the image needs no curl)
- Logs go to stdout; `URLET_LOG_FORMAT=json` pairs well with a collector such as Loki or
  CloudWatch
- Every request carries an `x-request-id` response header, and the same id is written to the log
- **Admin → Overview** in the admin UI shows the user count, short link count, total clicks and
  database size

## 12. Troubleshooting [#12-troubleshooting]

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
|---------|---------------|
| Startup fails with a migration checksum mismatch | A file in `migrations/` that was already applied has been edited; restore it or add a new migration instead |
| Signed out immediately after signing in | `URLET_BASE_URL` does not match the real URL, or `URLET_SECURE_COOKIES=true` while browsing over HTTP |
| Short links point at `http://localhost:8080` | `URLET_BASE_URL` is not set |
| `/health` returns 503 after the container starts | Volume permission problem: `/data` must be writable (the container runs as uid 10001) |
| Rate limits hit legitimate users (many users behind NAT) | Loosen the limits or switch those clients to API tokens; limits are counted per IP |
| Login returns 429 even with the correct password | The account is temporarily locked (30 failures within 15 minutes). Wait for the window to slide past, or run `sqlite3 /data/urlet.db "DELETE FROM login_attempts"` to clear it immediately |
| The CAPTCHA widget never appears | All four conditions must hold: a provider other than `none`, both keys, and the matching `ON_*` switch set to `true` |
| Every submission fails with `captcha_failed` | The secret key does not belong to the configured provider, the widget's hostname list does not include the domain users visit, or an API client forgot to send the widget token as `captcha_token` |
| The visitor solves the CAPTCHA but registration or sign-in still fails | The token was solved on a hostname that urlet does not accept: add it to `URLET_CAPTCHA_ALLOWED_HOSTNAMES` (the `WARN` log line names the reported hostname and the accepted candidates) |
| Want token access after forgetting the admin password | Resetting a password revokes every API token for that account (by design); create a new token afterwards |
| Forgot the admin password | The startup bootstrap runs only when **both** `URLET_ADMIN_EMAIL` and `URLET_ADMIN_PASSWORD` are non-empty, and for an account that already exists it merely promotes it to administrator — it does **not** change the password (the password is used only when the account does not exist yet). To recover, point `URLET_ADMIN_EMAIL` at another account you can still sign in to (any non-empty `URLET_ADMIN_PASSWORD` makes the bootstrap run), restart, and use that account; or overwrite the password hash directly with `sqlite3` |
| A short link expired and you want it back | Open `/app/urls/{id}` and extend it, or clear the expiry under "Edit settings"; the data was never deleted |
| Want to reuse a slug after deleting a short link | Deliberately not allowed (so old links cannot be hijacked); pick a new slug |

## 13. Security checklist [#13-security-checklist]

- [ ] `URLET_BASE_URL` uses `https://`
- [ ] `URLET_ADMIN_PASSWORD` is a strong password, changed at `/app/account` after the first sign-in
- [ ] `URLET_SECRET` is set (at least 32 random characters), or the auto-generated `secret.key` (0600) is backed up
- [ ] Only 80/443 are reachable from the internet. The base compose file publishes `${URLET_PORT:-8080}:8080` on every interface; the TLS overlay removes that publish, so use the overlay or firewall the port
- [ ] `URLET_TRUST_PROXY` matches the actual proxy behavior
- [ ] The registration mode is `invite` or `closed` (unless you really want open registration)
- [ ] `click_retention_days` and a backup schedule are planned
- [ ] A regular update routine exists (rebuild locally or pull a new `URLET_IMAGE` tag), with a
      backup before each upgrade
- [ ] Bot verification is enabled on registration and sign-in if the instance is reachable by the public internet


# Documentation (/en/docs)

urlet is a self-hosted URL shortener: one Rust binary and one SQLite file, with no external database, cache or frontend build step.

- [urlet deployment guide](/en/docs/deployment)
- [Themes](/en/docs/themes)
- [Multi-domain support](/en/docs/multi-domain)
- [urlet JSON API reference](/en/docs/api)


# Multi-domain support (/en/docs/multi-domain)

Status: implemented (shipped since v1.3.0)
Last updated: 2026-10-28

## 1. Summary [#1-summary]

urlet serves short links on one **canonical host** plus any number of **extra
domains**. The canonical host keeps the full application (`/`, `/app/*`,
`/api/v1/*`). Extra domains are redirect-only: they answer `GET /{slug}` and
`POST /{slug}/unlock`, render the theme-aware short landing page at `/`, and
send everything else back to the canonical host (or reject it).

Each domain owns its own slug namespace: `(domain_id, slug)` is unique. The same
slug may exist on `a.example.com` and `b.example.com` and resolve to different
targets.

## 2. Product decisions [#2-product-decisions]

| # | Decision | Choice |
|---|----------|--------|
| 1 | Extra-domain scope | Redirect-only. `/app/*` GET/HEAD → 308 to canonical; other methods → 404. `/api/v1/*` → 404 JSON. |
| 2 | Extra-domain root | The theme-aware short landing page (`noindex`) in all six themes, with the site tools (theme picker, language switcher); not the canonical marketing page and not a 404. |
| 3 | Default domain | Administrators may change it among active domains. The canonical host always exists and is always active, but need not be the default. |
| 4 | New domains | Created as `pending`; an administrator activates them after DNS/TLS is ready. Only `active` domains are selectable. |
| 5 | Scheme | One scheme for the whole instance, inherited from `URLET_BASE_URL`. No per-domain scheme column. |
| 6 | Public metadata API | Add an optional `?domain=<hostname>` parameter; omitted means the default domain. |
| 7 | Environment seed | `URLET_DOMAINS` inserts missing domains only; it never changes status, default or verification of existing rows. |

Implementation defaults agreed for the open points:

- Domains seeded through `URLET_DOMAINS` are inserted as `active` and verified:
  they are declared by the operator in deployment configuration.
- The short landing page is theme-aware (all six themes) and shows the site name,
  one explanatory sentence, a link to the canonical host and the site tools
  (theme picker, language switcher). No login, registration or slug input.
- The current default domain cannot be disabled or deleted until another active
  domain is made default.
- `domains.source` distinguishes `system`, `env` and `ui`. The system/canonical
  domain can be neither disabled nor deleted; environment-managed domains can be
  disabled but not deleted from the UI.

## 3. Host roles and routing [#3-host-roles-and-routing]

| Host | `/` | `/{slug}` | `/app/*` | `/api/v1/*` | `/health` |
|------|-----|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------|
| canonical | existing landing page | redirect | full app | full API | 200 |
| extra, `active` | theme-aware short landing page | redirect | GET/HEAD 308 to canonical; other methods 404 | 404 JSON | 200 |
| extra, `pending`/`disabled` | 404 | 404 | 404 | 404 JSON | 200 |
| unknown host | 404 | 404 | 404 | 404 JSON | 200 |

`/assets/*`, `/favicon.ico`, `/favicon.svg`, `/health` and `/healthz` bypass the
host gate so that error pages and container health checks keep working on every
host.

## 4. Data model [#4-data-model]

### `domains` [#domains]

Added by migration `0003_multi_domain`:

| Column | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `status` | `pending`, `active` or `disabled` |
| `source` | `system` (canonical), `env` (`URLET_DOMAINS`) or `ui` |
| `updated_at` | Last lifecycle change |

`hostname` is stored lower-case without a trailing dot and with an optional
non-default port. A `NOCASE` unique index backs case-insensitive lookups. The
existing `is_default` partial unique index keeps exactly one default domain.

### `urls` [#urls]

- `domain_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES domains(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT`
- `UNIQUE (domain_id, slug)` with the existing `COLLATE NOCASE` on `slug`
- legacy `NULL` values are back-filled to the default domain
- soft-deleted rows keep their `(domain_id, slug)` reservation

Migration `0005_group_domains` adds the per-group domain policy:
`user_groups.default_domain_id`, `restrict_domains` and the `group_domains`
allowlist decide each member's effective default and selectable domains.

## 5. Migration `0003_multi_domain` [#5-migration-0003_multi_domain]

Before renaming, the migration normalises hostnames into a temporary mapping and
merges rows that become identical (case, trailing dot, default port). The
survivor is the default row when the group has one, otherwise the lowest id;
`urls.domain_id` is remapped to it and duplicate rows are deleted. This handles
a v2 installation that changed `URLET_BASE_URL` from `example.com:443` to
`example.com` and therefore already had both rows.

SQLite cannot drop the inline `UNIQUE` on `urls.slug`, so the table is rebuilt
with the official 12-step procedure. Because `clicks`, `url_tags` and
`url_daily_stats` reference `urls` with `ON DELETE CASCADE`, the rebuild runs on
a dedicated connection with `PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF` **outside** the
transaction. The migration runner distinguishes transactional migrations from
rebuild migrations and always restores `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` before the
connection is closed. `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` must return no rows before
commit.

Before upgrading: back up the SQLite file. The migration has no down migration;
rollback is restoring the backup and the previous binary. Tests seed a v2
database with URLs, clicks, tags and daily stats, apply `0003`, and assert row
counts, foreign keys, back-filled domains, per-domain slug uniqueness and a
working `sqlite_sequence`.

## 6. Host resolution [#6-host-resolution]

- Read the `Host` header. An absent `Host` (HTTP/1.0 and tests) is treated as the
  canonical host. A present but undecodable/invalid `Host` is an unknown host.
